notes:
13 of 14 probes pass, nothing fails, and the one that did not run is a platform boundary rather than a gap. Plugin 0.45.3, Claude Code 2.1.263, mechanisms before the walk, no session limit. `real_agent` reads `partial` rather than `fail` for the first time: no probe failed against a real session.

The worktree lifecycle completed inside a certification run for the first time. A worktree was created, work was done in it, committed on its own branch, merged into the main checkout and the worktree removed -- `5a20ded GOLD-FEAT-001: document why decide_all takes today as an argument`, with the merge above it and nothing left behind. Both worktree probes pass on git's own record. Four releases of this plugin had made that impossible in three separate ways: a recorder registered on a provider hook prevented the creation, a branch guard reading the wrong directory refused the commit, and an untracked .claude/ meant the worktree had no organization in it at all.

The native task lifecycle and background execution pass too, so every execution and isolation mechanism this harness can reach is now exercised on real evidence.

What remains is one boundary and one piece of work. Teams have no CLI surface in 2.1.263, so `a-team-stage-carried-its-skills` cannot run at all and certification is correctly refused for it. And the walk still ends at REQ after three attempts, two REWORK decisions and an ESCALATE -- 7 of 11 predicates satisfied, with GOLD-REQ-001 unapproved, no NFR artifact, and the CYCLE-PROD rollup short of ACCEPTED.

Not canonical: two of seven required stages. But this is the first run where every question the harness could ask was answered, and the only unanswered one is a question the platform will not let it ask.
